_comment: Accepted findings. Everything in here is a known risk somebody has put
their name to, with a date on which the acceptance stops being valid.
The gate fails on a finding that is not listed, and it also fails on a
listed finding whose expiry has passed. That is the whole mechanism: an
exception nobody revisits becomes a build failure rather than a habit.
Fingerprint is project|rule|resource. Run scripts/scan.sh --print-new to
get the fingerprint for something you want to accept.

accepted.finding: Admin port 22 reachable from 0.0.0.0/0
accepted.reason: Teleport's own proxy listens on 3023-3026 and should be the only ingress. The port 22 rule is left over from the initial build and is not needed.

accepted.finding: IMDSv2 not pinned on the bastion
accepted.reason: Pre-dates the policy. Low exploitability while the host runs no untrusted workload, but it is a one-line fix.

accepted.finding: No VPC flow log
accepted.reason: Teleport records the sessions themselves, which is the higher-value audit trail. Flow logs are still wanted for AU-1.

accepted.finding: No VPC flow log on the drill VPC
accepted.reason: The drill VPC exists for roughly fifteen minutes per month and has no route to the internet. Flow logs would cost more than the drill.

accepted.finding: SNS topic not encrypted with a CMK
accepted.reason: Budget alerts carry account totals, not regulated data. Scheduled alongside the next KMS review.

accepted.finding: Unrestricted egress from the RDS security group
accepted.reason: Egress filtering on a database that has no route to the internet adds little. Wanted anyway for defence in depth, scheduled with the next module refresh.

accepted.finding: Subnets assign public IPs on launch
accepted.reason: The module ships public and private subnets; the finding is against the public tier, which is doing its job. Callers place workloads in the private tier.

accepted.finding: No VPC flow log in the shared VPC module
accepted.reason: Flow logs belong in the module rather than in every caller. Real gap against AU-1.

accepted.finding: S3 buckets are not versioned
accepted.reason: Versioning protects against accidental deletion and ransomware. Should be the module default.

accepted.finding: RDS IAM database authentication disabled
accepted.reason: Would remove a long-lived database password. Larger change than it looks because applications must be updated too.

accepted.finding: SNS topic not encrypted (trivy's view of the same issue as the policy finding above)
accepted.reason: Same underlying issue as the terraform.encryption finding. Both fingerprints are listed so either engine can be run alone.

accepted.finding: SSH open to the internet (trivy's view of the same issue as the policy finding)
accepted.reason: Duplicate of the terraform.network finding. The port 22 rule should simply be removed; Teleport listens on 3023-3026.

accepted.finding: IMDSv1 allowed on the bastion (trivy's view of the policy finding)
accepted.reason: Duplicate of the terraform.identity finding.

accepted.finding: Unencrypted root volume on the bastion
accepted.reason: The bastion holds session recordings before they are shipped, so this is data at rest. One-line fix.

accepted.finding: Unrestricted egress from the Teleport security group
accepted.reason: The proxy needs outbound for updates and the auth service. Should be narrowed to the endpoints it actually uses.

accepted.finding: Public subnet assigns public IPs
accepted.reason: The Teleport proxy is deliberately internet-facing; that is what it is for. The host behind it is not.

accepted.finding: Image not from a registry on the default trusted list
accepted.reason: The image is public.ecr.aws, which is AWS's own registry. The check's default allow-list does not include it. Policy configuration issue, not a finding.

accepted.finding: RDS encryption not enabled at instance level
accepted.reason: A snapshot restore inherits the source's encryption; it cannot be changed at restore time. Static analysis cannot see that, because the value depends on the snapshot. The drill should only ever be pointed at encrypted snapshots.

accepted.finding: Backup retention is zero
accepted.reason: Deliberate. This instance exists for about fifteen minutes and is itself a copy of a backup. Backing up a backup would cost money and protect nothing.

accepted.finding: Deletion protection disabled
accepted.reason: Deliberate, and load-bearing. The drill must be able to destroy this instance unattended. Deletion protection here would leave copies of production running.

accepted.finding: No VPC flow log (trivy's view of the same issue as the policy finding)
accepted.reason: Duplicate of the terraform.logging finding for this VPC. Both fingerprints are listed so either engine can run on its own.

accepted.finding: No VPC flow log on the drill VPC (trivy's view of the policy finding)
accepted.reason: Duplicate of the terraform.logging finding. The drill VPC lives for minutes and has no internet route.
